info.title: Extreme Networks Common Infrastructure API
info.description:
# Common Infrastructure REST API

This comprehensive API provides access to the Common Infrastructure services for Extreme Networks' network management platform. 
The API enables programmatic access to topology management, device management, service management, and network visualization capabilities.

## Key Features
- **Topology Management**: Retrieve and manage network topologies (physical, fabric, service layers)
- **Device Management**: Access device information, interfaces, neighbors, and fabric details
- **Service Management**: Manage L2/L3 VSN, VLAN, and VRF services
- **User Preferences**: Store and retrieve user-specific preferences
- **Real-time Updates**: WebSocket notifications for topology and device changes
- **Service Probing**: VLAN service probe utilities for network validation

## API Design
This API follows RESTful principles and supports JSON payloads. Most operations use POST methods with detailed criteria objects
to provide flexible filtering and querying capabilities suitable for complex network topologies.

## Authentication
This API is designed to be integrated with MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and other automation tools.
Authentication and authorization should be handled at the infrastructure level.

## MCP Server Integration
This API is optimized for MCP (Model Context Protocol) server integration with the following features:

**AI-Friendly Design:**
- Comprehensive endpoint descriptions with use cases and examples
- Structured error responses for better error handling
- Detailed parameter descriptions for automated API consumption
- Response schemas optimized for AI interpretation

**Automation Support:**
- API Key authentication recommended for MCP servers
- Asynchronous operations with proper status tracking
- Bulk operations where applicable
- Consistent data formats across endpoints

**Rate Limiting Considerations:**
- Recommended rate limit: 60 requests per minute
- Burst allowance: 10 requests
- Consider caching for topology and device data

## Rate Limiting
API calls should be rate-limited appropriately to prevent system overload, especially for large topology queries.

Retrieves comprehensive network topology data including nodes, edges, and custom positioning information.

This endpoint supports multiple topology types (physical, fabric, service) and view types (map, abstract, list).
The response includes hierarchical node structures with detailed device and group information, interconnection
data through edges, and user-customized positioning for visualization purposes.

**Use Cases:**
- Initial topology loading for network visualization
- Refreshing topology data after network changes
- Filtering topology by specific criteria (search, node states, etc.)
- Supporting different visualization views (map-based, abstract diagrams)

**Performance Considerations:**
- Large topologies may require pagination or filtering
- Consider using specific topology types to reduce response size
- Custom positions are cached and updated incrementally

post.description:
Selectively hides specific nodes or links from topology visualizations to improve diagram clarity,
reduce visual complexity, and create focused network views for specific analysis or presentation purposes.

This operation provides granular control over topology visibility, supporting:
- **Selective Hiding**: Hide individual nodes, links, or groups of network elements
- **View Customization**: Create simplified views for different audiences or use cases
- **Focus Management**: Reduce visual noise to highlight critical network paths or components
- **Presentation Support**: Generate clean topology diagrams for documentation or presentations
- **Troubleshooting Aid**: Hide non-relevant elements to focus on problem areas

**Hide Operation Details:**
- Hidden elements are removed from visual representation but remain in the data model
- Hide state is maintained per user session or can be made persistent
- Multiple elements can be hidden in a single operation
- Hidden elements can be restored using the unhide operation

**Use Cases:**
- Creating simplified network diagrams for executive presentations
- Focusing troubleshooting efforts on specific network segments
- Generating role-specific topology views (access layer, core, etc.)
- Reducing complexity for training and documentation purposes
- Supporting network change management workflows

**Operational Considerations:**
- Hide operations are reversible and non-destructive
- Hidden elements maintain their relationships and can affect path calculations
- Consider impact on topology analytics when hiding critical network elements

returning network elements to their normal display state and re-enabling their 
participation in visual analysis and interactive operations.

- **Bulk Operations**: Restore multiple hidden elements in a single request
- **State Management**: Manage visibility state across different topology views
- **Recovery Support**: Restore accidentally hidden critical network elements
- **View Completion**: Return to full topology visibility for comprehensive analysis

**Unhide Operation Details:**
- Restored elements immediately become visible in topology visualizations
- All relationships and connections are re-established in the visual representation
- Previously hidden elements retain their original positioning and properties
- Unhide operations can be applied to elements hidden in current or previous sessions

**Use Cases:**
- Recovering from accidental hide operations
- Transitioning from focused to comprehensive network views
- Restoring full topology visibility after targeted analysis
- Supporting dynamic visualization workflows
- Enabling collaborative topology analysis with shared visibility states

**Operational Considerations:**
- Unhide operations are immediate and affect real-time topology displays
- Consider performance impact when unhiding large numbers of elements

Retrieves user-specific preferences and configuration settings that personalize the network
management interface and customize the user experience across different application features.

This endpoint provides access to comprehensive user preference data including:
- **Interface Customization**: Dashboard layouts, widget configurations, and display preferences
- **Behavioral Settings**: Default views, auto-refresh intervals, and interaction preferences
- **Personalization Data**: Custom filters, saved searches, and bookmark configurations
- **Accessibility Options**: Display scaling, color themes, and accessibility accommodations
- **Feature Toggles**: User-specific feature enablement and experimental feature access

**Preference Categories:**
- **Visualization**: Topology view preferences, chart types, and display options
- **Workflow**: Default actions, confirmation settings, and automation preferences
- **Notifications**: Alert preferences, delivery methods, and escalation settings
- **Security**: Session management, authentication preferences, and privacy settings

**Use Cases:**
- Loading personalized user interface configurations on login
- Synchronizing user preferences across multiple sessions or devices
- Supporting user experience customization and accessibility requirements
- Enabling preference backup and restoration workflows
- Integration with single sign-on and identity management systems

**Data Management:**
- Preferences are stored per user and isolated between different user accounts
- Settings can be queried by specific keys or retrieved in bulk
- Preference data supports versioning and rollback capabilities

post.description:
Creates or updates user-specific preferences and configuration settings to personalize
the network management interface and maintain consistent user experience across sessions.

This endpoint enables comprehensive preference management including:
- **Preference Creation**: Establish new user-specific configuration settings
- **Preference Updates**: Modify existing settings while preserving unrelated preferences
- **Bulk Operations**: Create or update multiple preference items in a single request
- **Validation**: Ensure preference values conform to expected formats and constraints
- **Persistence**: Store preferences securely with appropriate user data protection

**Supported Preference Types:**
- **Interface Settings**: Layout configurations, theme selections, and display customizations
- **Operational Defaults**: Default time ranges, refresh intervals, and view preferences
- **Workflow Configurations**: Custom automation settings and process preferences
- **Security Preferences**: Session timeout preferences and security feature settings
- **Integration Settings**: Third-party tool integrations and API preferences

**Operation Characteristics:**
- **Atomic Updates**: All preferences in a request are updated together or none are updated
- **Merge Behavior**: New preferences are merged with existing ones, preserving unspecified settings
- **Validation**: Invalid preference values result in request rejection with detailed error information
- **Audit Trail**: Preference changes are logged for security and troubleshooting purposes

**Use Cases:**
- Saving user interface customizations and personal workflow configurations
- Implementing user onboarding and setup wizards
- Supporting preference import/export and migration workflows
- Enabling dynamic user experience optimization based on usage patterns
- Integration with user training and help systems

**Data Protection:**
- All preference data is encrypted and stored securely
- Preferences are isolated between users and protected by authentication
- Sensitive preference data is handled according to privacy and compliance requirements

delete.description:
Deletes specific user preferences to reset customizations, clean up obsolete settings,
or restore default application behavior for targeted preference categories.

This endpoint provides granular preference removal capabilities including:
- **Selective Deletion**: Remove specific preference keys while preserving others
- **Category Cleanup**: Delete entire preference categories or groups
- **Reset Functionality**: Restore specific settings to their default values
- **Data Cleanup**: Remove deprecated or invalid preference entries
- **Bulk Operations**: Delete multiple related preferences in a single operation

**Deletion Behavior:**
- **Targeted Removal**: Only preferences matching the specified key are deleted
- **Cascading Effects**: Related preferences may be affected based on dependencies
- **Default Restoration**: Deleted preferences revert to system or application defaults
- **Audit Logging**: Deletion operations are logged for security and troubleshooting
- **Validation**: Ensures critical system preferences cannot be accidentally deleted

**Use Cases:**
- Resetting user interface to default settings for troubleshooting
- Cleaning up user accounts during offboarding or role changes
- Removing obsolete preferences after application updates
- Supporting user-initiated preference reset workflows
- Enabling preference troubleshooting and support scenarios
- Data privacy compliance and user data management

**Safety Considerations:**
- **Irreversible Operation**: Deleted preferences cannot be automatically recovered
- **Backup Recommendation**: Consider backing up preferences before deletion
- **Impact Assessment**: Deletion may affect user experience and require reconfiguration
- **Dependency Validation**: System checks for preference dependencies before deletion

**Data Protection:**
- Deletion operations are authenticated and authorized per user
- Audit trails maintain records of preference deletion for compliance
- Secure deletion ensures preference data cannot be recovered inappropriately

Creates or updates custom positioning data for network elements in topology visualizations,
enabling users to maintain consistent, personalized network diagram layouts that enhance
understanding and presentation of network infrastructure.

This endpoint provides comprehensive position management capabilities including:
- **Element Positioning**: Define precise X,Y coordinates for nodes and network elements
- **Layout Persistence**: Save custom arrangements that persist across sessions and users
- **Multi-View Support**: Maintain different positioning schemes for various topology views
- **Collaborative Layouts**: Share positioning schemes across teams or user groups
- **Dynamic Updates**: Modify positions in real-time during interactive topology sessions

**Positioning Features:**
- **Coordinate Systems**: Support for various coordinate systems and scaling factors
- **Element Relationships**: Maintain relative positioning and alignment between connected elements
- **Layout Templates**: Create reusable positioning patterns for similar network structures
- **Constraint Handling**: Respect positioning constraints and collision detection
- **Version Control**: Track changes to positioning schemes over time

**Use Cases:**
- Creating standardized network documentation with consistent element placement
- Maintaining logical network diagrams that reflect physical or functional relationships
- Supporting collaborative network design and planning sessions
- Enabling presentation-ready topology views for executive reporting
- Facilitating network training and educational material development
- Integration with network design tools and documentation systems

**Performance Considerations:**
- Position updates are processed efficiently for real-time interactive use
- Bulk position updates are optimized for large topology modifications
- Position data is cached for quick retrieval and rendering performance
- Consider network complexity when updating large numbers of element positions

**Data Management:**
- Custom positions are associated with specific topology views and chart contexts
- Position data includes metadata for validation and troubleshooting
- Support for position inheritance and template-based positioning

delete.description:
Deletes custom positioning data for specific topology views, resetting network elements
to their default algorithmic positions and cleaning up personalized layout configurations.

This operation provides comprehensive position data cleanup including:
- **View-Specific Deletion**: Remove custom positions for specific topology chart contexts
- **Selective Reset**: Target specific topology views while preserving others
- **Layout Cleanup**: Remove obsolete or corrupted positioning data
- **Default Restoration**: Return elements to automatic layout algorithm positioning
- **Data Maintenance**: Clean up positioning data during system maintenance or migration

**Deletion Behavior:**
- **Targeted Removal**: Only positions associated with the specified chart hash are deleted
- **Automatic Fallback**: Elements immediately revert to default algorithmic positioning
- **Cascading Effects**: Related positioning constraints and relationships are also removed
- **Performance Optimization**: Deletion operation is optimized for minimal disruption
- **Audit Trail**: Deletion operations are logged for troubleshooting and recovery

**Use Cases:**
- Resetting topology layouts to default algorithmic positioning
- Cleaning up corrupted or invalid positioning data
- Supporting topology view maintenance and optimization workflows
- Enabling layout troubleshooting and problem resolution
- Facilitating topology migration and system upgrades
- Supporting user interface reset and recovery scenarios

**Recovery Considerations:**
- **Irreversible Operation**: Deleted position data cannot be automatically recovered
- **Layout Recreation**: Users will need to manually recreate custom positioning if needed
- **Impact Assessment**: Consider user workflow impact before deleting established layouts
- **Alternative Approaches**: Consider exporting position data before deletion for backup

**Performance Impact:**
- Deletion operations are processed efficiently with minimal system impact
- Topology views are automatically refreshed with default positioning
- Related caching and rendering systems are updated to reflect position changes

get.description:
Retrieves comprehensive physical link information including port utilization statistics, 
traffic counters, error statistics, and operational details for both ends of a network link.

This endpoint provides detailed insights into:
- **Utilization Metrics**: Current and maximum bandwidth utilization percentages
- **Traffic Statistics**: Packet and byte counters for unicast, broadcast, and multicast traffic
- **Error Statistics**: Various error counters including discards, CRC errors, collisions
- **Port Details**: Administrative and operational states, speed, duplex, media type
- **LAG Information**: For aggregated links, includes member port details and protocols

**Use Cases:**
- Network performance monitoring and troubleshooting
- Capacity planning and bandwidth analysis
- Link health assessment and error detection
- Integration with network monitoring systems

**Performance Impact:**
- Statistics are collected in real-time from network devices
- Response time depends on device responsiveness and network latency

get.description:
Retrieves comprehensive Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) and Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP)
neighbor information, providing essential network discovery data for topology mapping,
connectivity validation, and network documentation workflows.

This endpoint provides detailed neighbor discovery information including:
- **Protocol Support**: Both LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) and CDP neighbor discovery data
- **Neighbor Identity**: Device names, system descriptions, and management addresses
- **Connection Details**: Local and remote port information, interface mappings, and link characteristics
- **Capability Information**: Discovered device capabilities, supported protocols, and system features
- **Network Context**: VLAN information, network policies, and service advertisements

**Discovery Protocol Features:**
- **Multi-Protocol Support**: Unified view of LLDP and CDP discovery information
- **Real-Time Data**: Current neighbor states with timestamp and aging information
- **Detailed Attributes**: Extended device information including software versions and serial numbers
- **Topology Correlation**: Neighbor data correlation with topology discovery and validation
- **Change Detection**: Neighbor changes, additions, and removals with historical context

**Neighbor Information Categories:**
- **Device Identification**: System names, descriptions, chassis IDs, and management addresses
- **Interface Mapping**: Local and remote port details, interface descriptions, and connection types
- **Network Services**: Advertised VLANs, network policies, and service capabilities
- **System Capabilities**: Router, switch, bridge, access point, and other device role information
- **Protocol Details**: Discovery protocol versions, TLV extensions, and vendor-specific information

**Use Cases:**
- Network topology discovery and automated mapping workflows
- Connectivity validation and link verification processes
- Network documentation and cable management systems
- Troubleshooting connectivity issues and layer 2 problems
- Integration with network discovery tools and topology databases
- Supporting network audit and compliance verification
- Device replacement and migration planning

**Data Accuracy Considerations:**
- Neighbor data accuracy depends on device support for LLDP/CDP protocols
- Discovery information reflects the most recent protocol exchanges
- Some devices may have discovery protocols disabled for security reasons
- Neighbor aging and timeout values affect data freshness and reliability

post.description:
Initiates a comprehensive VLAN service probe operation to validate VLAN availability and configuration
across the network infrastructure. This utility performs automated testing to determine which VLANs
are properly configured, accessible, and functional on the specified device.

**Probe Operation Details:**
- **VLAN Discovery**: Automatically detects configured VLANs within the specified range
- **Connectivity Testing**: Validates VLAN reachability and proper forwarding
- **Configuration Validation**: Checks VLAN settings, tagging, and port assignments
- **IP Address Assignment**: Tests dynamic IP assignment capabilities (DHCP)
- **Gateway Verification**: Validates default gateway accessibility per VLAN

**Use Cases:**
- **Network Commissioning**: Validate VLAN configuration during initial setup
- **Troubleshooting**: Identify VLAN connectivity issues and misconfigurations
- **Compliance Verification**: Ensure VLAN setup meets network policies
- **Change Management**: Verify VLAN functionality after configuration changes
- **Documentation**: Generate current VLAN availability reports

**Operational Considerations:**
- Probe operations are non-disruptive to production traffic
- Maximum of 500 VLANs can be probed in a single operation
- Concurrent probe operations on the same device are not allowed
- Results are cached and available for retrieval during and after completion

**Progress Tracking:**
Use the returned `taskKey` to monitor progress via the `/utilities/service-probe-vlan/probe-data` endpoint.

post.description:
Terminates an active VLAN service probe operation, gracefully stopping the validation
process and cleaning up allocated resources while preserving any results collected
up to the point of termination.

This endpoint provides comprehensive probe termination capabilities including:
- **Graceful Termination**: Stop ongoing probe operations without data corruption
- **Resource Cleanup**: Release network resources and probe-related system allocations
- **Result Preservation**: Maintain partial probe results for analysis and reporting
- **State Management**: Update probe operation status and completion tracking
- **Audit Trail**: Log termination actions for compliance and troubleshooting

**Termination Scenarios:**
- **Manual Termination**: User-initiated stop for probe operations that are no longer needed
- **Timeout Prevention**: Stop long-running probes before system timeout limits
- **Resource Management**: Terminate probes to free resources for other operations
- **Error Recovery**: Stop malfunctioning or stuck probe operations
- **Maintenance Preparation**: Clear active probes before system maintenance

**Operation Characteristics:**
- **Immediate Response**: Stop commands are processed immediately with confirmation
- **Safe Termination**: Probe operations are stopped safely without affecting network stability
- **Result Availability**: Partial results remain accessible after termination
- **Resource Recovery**: Network interfaces and system resources are properly released
- **Status Updates**: Probe status is updated to reflect termination state

**Use Cases:**
- Stopping probe operations that have completed their intended validation
- Terminating long-running probes that exceed expected completion times
- Freeing network resources when probe operations are no longer required
- Recovering from probe operations that appear to be stuck or malfunctioning
- Preparing for network maintenance by clearing active validation operations
- Supporting probe lifecycle management and operational workflows
- Implementing probe timeout and resource management policies
- Enabling responsive probe operation control for network administrators

**Post-Termination Actions:**
- **Result Retrieval**: Use the probe-data endpoint to retrieve partial results
- **Resource Verification**: Confirm that network resources have been properly released
- **Status Monitoring**: Verify that probe status reflects the terminated state
- **Cleanup Validation**: Ensure that no residual probe processes remain active

**Operational Safeguards:**
- **Confirmation Required**: Termination requires explicit confirmation to prevent accidental stops
- **Impact Assessment**: System validates that termination will not affect other operations
- **Recovery Support**: Terminated probes can be restarted if needed
- **Audit Logging**: All termination actions are logged for operational tracking

- **Progress Information**: Real-time status updates and completion progress
- **Connectivity Analysis**: VLAN reachability, configuration validation, and performance metrics
- **Error Diagnostics**: Detailed error information for failed VLAN validations

**Data Retrieval Options:**
- **Task-Based Retrieval**: Get results for a specific probe operation using task key
- **Device-Based Retrieval**: Get all probe results associated with a specific device

- **Successful Validations**: VLANs that passed all connectivity and configuration tests
- **Failed Validations**: VLANs with connectivity issues, configuration problems, or access failures
- **Partial Results**: VLANs with mixed validation outcomes or incomplete testing
- **Pending Tests**: VLANs currently being tested or queued for validation
- **Skipped Tests**: VLANs excluded from testing due to configuration or policy constraints

**Detailed Analysis Data:**
- **VLAN Configuration**: Detected VLAN settings, tagging, and port assignments
- **Connectivity Metrics**: Response times, packet loss, and reachability statistics
- **DHCP Analysis**: IP address assignment testing and DHCP server responsiveness
- **Gateway Validation**: Default gateway accessibility and routing verification
- **Quality Metrics**: Network performance indicators and service quality assessments

- Generating network validation reports and compliance documentation
- Supporting network troubleshooting workflows with detailed diagnostic data
- Integration with network monitoring and alerting systems

- Providing evidence for network service level agreement compliance
- Enabling automated network validation and quality assurance processes

**Data Format and Structure:**
- **Structured Results**: Organized data format optimized for analysis and reporting
- **Timestamp Information**: Detailed timing data for probe operations and individual tests
- **Error Classification**: Categorized error information with diagnostic details
- **Performance Baselines**: Comparative data for performance trend analysis
- **Export Capabilities**: Data formatted for integration with external systems and tools

**Real-Time Monitoring:**
- **Live Updates**: Real-time progress information for ongoing probe operations
- **Status Indicators**: Current probe state, completion percentage, and estimated time remaining
- **Incremental Results**: Progressive result availability as individual VLAN tests complete
- **Error Notifications**: Immediate visibility into probe errors and validation failures

**Historical Analysis:**

- **Baseline Establishment**: Create performance and connectivity baselines for future comparisons

TopologyCriteria.description:
Comprehensive criteria object for topology retrieval operations. This schema defines all possible
filters, preferences, and options for customizing topology queries to meet specific visualization
and analysis requirements.

**Key Features:**
- **Multi-layer Support**: Query across physical, fabric, and service topology layers
- **Flexible Filtering**: Advanced search and filtering capabilities
- **Visualization Options**: Support for different view types and layouts
- **Service Integration**: Service-specific topology features
- **Performance Optimization**: Pagination and selective data loading

GeneralCriteria.description:
Primary criteria object for topology operations defining the core parameters for data retrieval
and visualization preferences. This schema controls the fundamental aspects of how topology
data is queried, filtered, and presented.

**Topology Types:**
- **physical**: Physical layer topology showing actual hardware connections
- **fabric**: Fabric layer topology showing logical fabric connections (SPBM, EVPN)
- **service**: Service layer topology showing L2/L3 services and their relationships
- **accessLayer**: Simplified view focusing on access layer devices
- **physicalAndFabric**: Combined view showing both physical and fabric layers

**View Types:**
- **map**: Geographic or floor plan based visualization
- **abstract**: Logical diagram representation
- **list**: Tabular or list-based presentation

**Actions:**
- **expand**: Expand a collapsed group or node to show children
- **collapse**: Collapse an expanded group to hide children
- **collapse-all**: Collapse all expanded groups in the topology
- **snapshot**: Capture current topology state for comparison
- **search**: Perform search-based filtering

nodeID.description:
UUID of the specific node (device or group) on which to focus the topology operation.

**Use Cases:**
- Expand/collapse operations on specific groups
- Center topology view on a particular building or floor
- Filter topology to show only descendants of a specific node
- Access layer topology scoped to a specific building

**Node Types:**
- Building IDs for access layer topology
- Group IDs for hierarchical operations
- Device IDs for device-centric views

connectedState.description:

in the UI. Used to maintain visual context and selection states across topology updates.

**Purpose:**
- Preserve user selections during topology refresh
- Maintain visual highlighting and focus
- Support multi-node operations and comparisons

DeviceType.description:
Classification of network devices based on their primary function and role in the network infrastructure.
This enumeration helps categorize devices for appropriate management, monitoring, and visualization.

**Infrastructure Devices:**
- **switch**: Layer 2/3 network switches (access, distribution, core)
- **router**: IP routers for Layer 3 routing and WAN connectivity
- **bridge**: Network bridges for Layer 2 connectivity

**Wireless Infrastructure:**
- **accessPoint**: Wireless access points for Wi-Fi connectivity
- **repeater**: Wireless repeaters and range extenders

**WAN and Edge:**
- **sdWan**: SD-WAN edge devices and controllers

**End Devices:**
- **server**: Physical and virtual servers
- **laptop**: Laptop computers and mobile workstations
- **tablet**: Tablet devices and mobile computing devices
- **mobile**: Mobile phones and handheld devices

**IP-Enabled Devices:**
- **ipCamera**: IP security cameras and surveillance equipment
- **ipPhone**: VoIP phones and unified communications devices
- **telephone**: Traditional telephony equipment

**Logical and Service Entities:**
- **ipClientService**: IP-based client services and applications
- **internet**: Internet gateway or external connectivity representation

**Device Classification Notes:**
- Classification may be automatically detected or manually assigned
- Some devices may have multiple functions but are classified by primary role
- Device type affects available management operations and monitoring capabilities
- Used for filtering, grouping, and applying type-specific policies
